chief_complaint: high fever, perineal pain, and exquisitely tender boggy prostate
hpi_details: A 26-year-old male presents to the clinic with high fever, perineal pain, and exquisitely tender boggy prostate. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening.
ideas: He thinks he caught a bad bladder infection or picked up a bug from using the gym sauna.
concerns: He is worried that the severe infection might cause permanent damage to his fertility and ability to have children.
expectations: He hopes to get strong antibiotics and pain medication so he can sit and urinate without severe pain.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Bacterial Prostatitis evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Bacterial Prostatitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes prompt empiric antibiotics covering both typical uropathogens and, in sexually active young men, STI organisms (N. gonorrhoeae/C. trachomatis), then narrowing based on culture, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: high fever, perineal pain, and exquisitely tender boggy prostate

Key HPI features: A 26-year-old male presents to the clinic with high fever, perineal pain, and exquisitely tender boggy prostate. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening.

Objective/Exam findings: Fever, tachycardia; assess for hypotension/sepsis. Gentle digital rectal exam (avoid vigorous palpation/massage) reveals an exquisitely tender, boggy, warm prostate. Suprapubic exam for bladder distension suggesting urinary retention. No scrotal swelling or tenderness to suggest epididymo-orchitis.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Bacterial Prostatitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Urinary tract infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute total urinary retention.
management_principles: Screen for systemic sepsis and urinary retention; if retention occurs, use a suprapubic catheter rather than urethral catheterization to avoid worsening the prostatic infection
Obtain urine culture, blood cultures if febrile/toxic, and STI testing (gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT) given the patient's age and sexual history; avoid vigorous prostate massage/examination

Start empiric antibiotics promptly covering both typical uropathogens and, in sexually active young men, N. gonorrhoeae/C. trachomatis, per local antibiogram and STI risk, then narrow based on culture
Admit for IV antibiotics if systemically unwell or in retention; complete a total 2-4 week course, and reassess for abscess or chronic prostatitis if symptoms persist.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of high fever, perineal pain, and exquisitely tender boggy prostate.
reference_soap.objective: Fever, tachycardia; assessed for hypotension/sepsis. Gentle digital rectal exam reveals an exquisitely tender, boggy, warm prostate. No bladder distension. No scrotal swelling or tenderness.
reference_soap.assessment: Acute bacterial prostatitis; given the patient's age, both typical uropathogens and sexually transmitted organisms (N. gonorrhoeae, C. trachomatis) must be considered.
reference_soap.plan: Obtain urine culture, blood cultures if febrile/toxic, and STI testing (gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT). Avoid prostate massage. Start empiric antibiotics covering typical uropathogens and STI organisms per local antibiogram, admitting for IV therapy if systemically unwell or in urinary retention (using a suprapubic catheter if retention occurs), and complete a total 2-4 week course once stable.

must_ask.say: When did the fever start, and how high has it been?
Can you describe the pain you're feeling between your legs and rectum?
Do you have burning with urination, or any difficulty starting your stream?
Have you had any new sexual partners recently, and do you use protection?
Do you feel very weak, confused, or like your heart is racing along with the fever?

history.answer: I have been having a really high fever and terrible, deep pain down between my legs around my groin.
It started about three days ago with a dull ache down below, and over the past day or two the fever spiked and the pain got much worse.
My thermometer at home read up to 39 degrees Celsius this morning. I've had shaking chills and severe sweats that wake me up.
It feels like a heavy, throbbing ache deep in my perineum, right between my scrotum and anus. It hurts worse when I sit down or try to push out urine.
I took some acetaminophen yesterday. It brought the fever down a tiny bit for a couple of hours, but then the high fever and chills came roaring back.
Yes, it burns intensely every time I pee, and I feel like I have to run to the bathroom every half hour even when only a small trickle comes out.
The stream is very weak and hesitates before starting. I feel like I can't empty my bladder completely, but I am still able to get some urine out.
No, my urine looks a bit cloudy, but I haven't seen any visible red blood in it.
No, I don't have any pain in my mid-back, flanks, or sides.
No cough, phlegm, runny nose, or sore throat at all. My chest feels completely clear.
No nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, or diarrhea. My bowels have been regular, though it hurts my pelvic floor when I bear down.
I have a slight headache from the high fever, but my neck isn't stiff, and I am not confused or drowsy.
I feel very weak and tired from the fever, but I haven't felt dizzy, faint, or short of breath when standing up.
No, I have not noticed any rash, spots, or bug bites anywhere on my body, and my joints don't hurt.
No, I haven't had chronic night sweats or unexplained weight loss before this started three days ago.
No, I haven't felt any swollen lumps or glands in my neck, armpits, or groin.
No, I haven't traveled abroad recently, haven't been hiking in the woods or fields, and don't have contact with animals.
No, everyone at home and at work has been feeling completely healthy.
I started seeing a new sexual partner about three weeks ago, and we had unprotected intercourse. I haven't had any visible penile sores or discharge that I noticed.
No, I have never injected drugs or used illicit substances.
I have been completely healthy my whole life. No high blood pressure, diabetes, or kidney issues.
No past surgeries, and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescribed medications, over-the-counter drugs, or nutritional supplements regularly.
No, I don't have any known allergies to foods or medications.
No chemotherapy, steroids, or any immunosuppressive treatments. My immune system has always been normal.
No, my heart is completely fine, and I haven't had any dental work or medical procedures done recently.
No, I haven't started any new medications before getting sick.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I drink a beer or two with friends once or twice a month, but that's about it.
I work as an office software developer and live in an apartment in the city.
No major illnesses run in my family. Neither of my parents has had early prostate or kidney problems.
I thought maybe I picked up a nasty bladder bug from the sauna at my gym.
I'm really scared that this infection might permanently mess up my chances of having kids.
I'm hoping you can prescribe some strong antibiotics and painkillers so I can actually sit down and pee without agony.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, heart rate 104 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, body temperature 38.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on ambient air.
No pharyngeal erythema, tonsillar exudate, or mucosal ulcerations.
No cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary lymphadenopathy.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally with no crackles, wheezes, or rhonchi.
Tachycardic regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2, with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Soft, non-distended abdomen with mild tenderness above the pubic bone, but no palpable bladder distension, rebound tenderness, or organomegaly.
Normal external genitalia without urethral discharge, scrotal swelling, erythema, or testicular/epididymal tenderness.
Extremely tender, markedly swollen, boggy, and warm prostate on gentle palpation; examination terminated promptly without vigorous massage.
No neck stiffness; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
No skin rashes, petechiae, purpura, or insect bites/eschar noted.
